clue.text: Archbishop Welby faces issue, returning with seconds to spare

parts.note: Justin Welby was Archbishop of Canterbury

indicators.note: returning means the word for issue is read backwards

parts.note: to issue is to emit

explanation.surface: The Archbishop confronts a problem and comes back just before a deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faces' is only a link word here, and Welby's first name is the piece needed; 'returning' signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: arriving with seconds to spare means arriving barely before the deadline.

clue.text: Part of doorway to get stuck reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that we hear a word that sounds like the one for getting stuck

parts.note: to jam is to get stuck, as a door may

explanation.surface: A piece of the doorframe is said to stick.
explanation.definitionFit: The upright side post of a door frame is called by this name.

clue.text: Member of government involved in treason

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters of treason are tangled together into a new order

explanation.surface: A politician is implicated in a plot against the state.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a legislator, a member of a senate that governs.

clue.text: Those lacking ability nicest, top men horrible

indicators.note: horrible suggests the letters of nicest and top men are made a mess of and rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that the nicest men in charge are dreadful at their jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: People lacking ability are unskilled, inept people: a plural noun for the useless.

clue.text: Tramline runs out here

indicators.note: runs out suggests the letters of tramline escape and run into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A tram route ends at this point.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the tramline's letters rearrange, and a tramline does end at a depot like this.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus where a transport route ends is called this kind of station.

clue.text: Crazy about the female and reduced to pulp

indicators.note: about means the word for crazy goes around the pronoun

parts.note: crazy means mad
she is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: Someone is mad about a woman and has been crushed to pulp by it.
explanation.definitionFit: Food reduced to pulp has been crushed soft, as potatoes are.

clue.text: Hands back something that has been exchanged

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for hands backwards

parts.note: paws is a jocular word for hands

explanation.surface: Someone hands back an item that was traded.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade or exchange is a noun synonym; the thing exchanged is itself called this.

clue.text: Rapid motion has you upsetting drink

parts.note: a whisk is a quick sweeping movement

indicators.note: upsetting means turning the old word for you upside down, in a down clue reading it backwards

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: A fast movement causes you to spill your drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish or American spirit distilled from grain is a type of drink.

clue.text: Exciting work, one appreciated by the organist?

definitions.meaning: a gripping book that keeps you reading
an assistant who flips the pages of the music for a player at the keyboard

explanation.surface: A thrilling composition, and the helper an organist values.
explanation.definitionFit: A gripping novel is called this, and so is the assistant who flips an organist's sheet music.

clue.text: Maiden is hidden by fancy curtain, someone in the beauty business

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for maiden over

indicators.note: hidden by means the little word is tucked inside the jumbled letters
fancy suggests the letters of curtain are elaborately rearranged

explanation.surface: A young woman conceals herself behind an ornate curtain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' turns CURTAIN into ANICURT; 'hidden by' puts IS into it to give ANICURIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A beautician who tends hands and nails works in the beauty trade.

clue.text: Phone round

definitions.meaning: to call someone on the telephone

explanation.definitionFit: To call on the telephone is to give a buzz; a circle is a band of this shape.

clue.text: What interviewee for job hopes to be, in a position where competitors are in a line

definitions.text: What interviewee for job hopes to be
definitions.meaning: a candidate hopes to be starting in a new job, read as two words

definitions.text: a position where competitors are in a line
definitions.meaning: the marker where runners line up at the start of a race

explanation.surface: A job candidate hopes to be lined up like racers at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the phrase as 'starting (a) post', i.e. beginning a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A racecourse mark where horses line up, and a candidate's hope of beginning a new job.

clue.text: Check something growing up in garden?

definitions.meaning: a plant stalk rising from the soil

explanation.surface: A query about stopping something that is shooting up in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop a flow is to staunch it; a plant's upright stalk grows from the soil.

clue.text: Like a formulaic pattern I repeatedly knitted badly

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters of the pair and knitted are put together wrongly
repeatedly means the letter I is taken twice

explanation.surface: A knitter confesses to messing up a stock pattern again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles I; 'badly' shuffles II with KNITTED.
explanation.definitionFit: A composite face picture built from stock features, hence anything formulaic and stereotyped.

clue.text: Bullish little man is twitching after work

indicators.note: after means the man, is and twitch follow the word for work

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
Tim, as in Tiny Tim, a little fellow
a tic is a twitch

explanation.surface: A small man is jumpy after a job, though confident.
explanation.definitionFit: In market talk bullish means hopeful that prices will rise; generally confident.

clue.text: Cheese and pears man chewed

indicators.note: chewed suggests the letters of pears and man are mashed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man eats a snack of cheese with pears.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard Italian cheese, an example of the category.

clue.text: Bit of light comes in through devotional exercise

indicators.note: comes in means the beam goes inside the word for through

parts.note: per means through or by
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A beam of light shines through during worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking to God is a devotional act, an example of religious exercise.

clue.text: Fundamental level of interest in the banking world

parts.note: base means fundamental, at bottom
a rate is a level, as of pay

explanation.surface: The basic interest rate set by banks.
explanation.definitionFit: The central bank's lending rate of interest on which other bank rates are based.

clue.text: Trendy exploit that surprises me

parts.note: in means fashionable
a deed is a feat or exploit

explanation.surface: A fashionable stunt that astonishes the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: An interjection of surprise: 'really!' says something astonishes the speaker.

clue.text: Stylish ring remains hidden

indicators.note: hidden means the burnt remains are concealed inside the bell sound

parts.note: ding is the sound of a bell ringing
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A smart ring stays out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashing describes someone attractively smart and spirited in appearance.

clue.text: He can sing over a range except for one tricky note

definitions.text: He can sing over a range

parts.note: bar means except, as in 'all bar one'
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters of note are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A singer can cover a range of notes apart from one difficult one.
explanation.definitionFit: A male singer whose voice lies between tenor and bass, covering a particular range.

clue.text: Actor, the first person to appear in a musical

indicators.note: to appear in means the pronoun goes inside the show's title

parts.note: Oliver! is Lionel Bart's musical
I is the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: An actor was the first to be cast in a stage musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was a celebrated English stage and film actor.

clue.text: Bitter substance girl put in can

indicators.note: put in means the girl's name goes inside the word for can

parts.note: a tin is a can
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl puts something bitter into a can.
explanation.definitionFit: An astringent compound in tea and wine bark, giving a bitter taste.

clue.text: At home one day I had a meal, not completely filled up

parts.note: in means at home
Sat is short for Saturday
ate means had a meal

explanation.surface: Someone eats at home but is still left a little hungry.
explanation.definitionFit: Insatiate means never satisfied, so never completely filled.

clue.text: Excellent silver brought back for goddess

indicators.note: brought back means the two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, with the 1 read as I
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Fine silver returned to a goddess's shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaia is the Greek earth goddess.

clue.text: Sort of farm boss

definitions.meaning: a farm where horses are bred

explanation.definitionFit: A breeding farm for horses, and a raised knob or nailhead, which is what a boss is.

clue.text: Work in small room — waste of energy and time

indicators.note: waste of means the energy and time letters are lost

parts.note: toilet, the smallest room in the house
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Working in a tiny room squanders effort and hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Toil is hard labour, a synonym for work.

clue.text: Worker with muscle — bolshy type?

parts.note: an ant is a worker insect
an agonist is a muscle whose contraction moves a part

explanation.surface: A burly worker who is difficult and rebellious.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bolshy is combative and contrary, an opponent or adversary type.

clue.text: Composer, his first bit taking time

definitions.text: Composer, his first bit taking time

indicators.note: taking means the opening letter takes on the word for time after it
his first bit refers to the opening letter of the word composer

parts.note: an age is a long time

explanation.surface: A composer's opening piece takes a long while.
explanation.walkthrough: The composer's own initial plus AGE spells his name; famously John Cage's 4'33" is all about time.
explanation.definitionFit: John Cage was an American avant-garde composer.

clue.text: Illiterate, showing no sign of any clues solved here?

definitions.text: showing no sign of any clues solved here?
definitions.meaning: an empty grid with no letters entered

explanation.surface: An uneducated solver whose grid stays blank.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking learning, and literally without letters, as an empty crossword grid is.
